cards.headline: White House says Melania Trump secured ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Ukraine

pages.text: The White House has announced that U.S. First Lady Melania Trump has successfully secured a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky. According to the White House, the truce is scheduled to begin on 29 October, though neither Russia nor Ukraine has commented on the announcement. A senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that a ceasefire in the city would be established soon, while Russia has not provided a response. Neither party has confirmed the terms of the agreement. Oleshky, located in the Kherson region, was captured by Russian forces during the first week of the full-scale invasion in February 2022. While the city had a pre-war population of 24,000, an estimated 2,000 residents remain under Russian rule. The White House described the city as a front-line war city on the brink of disaster, noting that residents have faced limited electricity, mined roads, regular military attacks, and a lack of gas since 2023. Recent reports indicated that some remaining residents have resorted to eating garden weeds to survive due to food and water shortages.

In a statement released by the White House, Melania Trump said she worked directly with both Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localized ceasefire. She stated that without her intervention, the possibility of bringing humanitarian aid into the city and evacuating the elderly would have been impossible. The plan involves non-military, civilian leaders from both countries working together to visit residents in their homes to determine required assistance. The First Lady noted that residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to a preferred destination, with the option to choose either Russia or Ukraine. This development follows previous efforts by the First Lady, who has focused on helping children in conflict and reportedly used backchannel communications with Vladimir Putin last year to assist in reuniting displaced or abducted children with their families.

cards.headline: Scientists warn heat killed 50,000 people in European cities this summer

pages.text: New research suggests that heat killed a record 50,000 people in European cities during the summer months of June to August. Scientists reported that the death toll was the worst on record, with the hot weather killing nearly twice as many people as it did in each of the two next most dangerous years. The study, which modeled historical relationships between heat and health across 854 cities, attributed two in every three of the deaths to climate breakdown. Researchers found that heat added by pollution cut short an extra 32,000 lives in urban areas. Malcolm Mistry, a climate and health scientist at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and co-author of the study, described the absolute numbers of estimated heat-related deaths across the 854 urban areas as “staggering.” Mistry noted that the proportion of deaths attributed to anthropogenic climate change has risen from approximately 40% at the start of the century to 65% this summer. The study found that people succumbed to heat at the highest rates in Malta, Italy, and Hungary, while the greatest absolute death tolls occurred in Italy, France, Spain, Germany, and the UK. In the UK, scientists estimated 4,354 heat deaths this summer, a figure noted by Katie White, the UK climate transition minister. In Naples, Italy, the study's age-standardised estimates indicated that 815 people per million died from the heat. Mario Guarino, an emergency doctor at Ospedale CTO in northern Naples, reported a 15% increase in emergency room visits during the hottest weeks, citing the complexity of health problems exacerbated by heat alongside factors such as loneliness and poverty.

pages.text: President Donald Trump signed legislation on Tuesday to establish Chiricahua National Park in south-eastern Arizona, making it the 64th national park in the United States. The 19-square-mile (49-square-km) site, known among Native Americans as the Land of Standing-Up Rocks, was designated a national monument in the 1920s to preserve pinnacle-shaped rocks formed by an ancient volcanic eruption. The bill passed Congress with bipartisan support. 1920s-era designation was intended to protect the hundreds of rock spires that characterize the landscape. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum stated that the area's rock spires, biodiversity, and Apache heritage make it an extraordinary landscape that will create opportunities to strengthen local economies and welcome visitors. The site is located within the historical territory of the Chiricahua Apache tribes, who resided there for centuries before surrendering to US troops in 1886 and being forcibly removed to the San Carlos Apache reservation. pages.text: A World Bank report states that money supply outpacing production growth in Bangladesh is fueling inflation, as government borrowing creates a liquidity surge while private-sector credit flow slows amid production deceleration. According to the report, broad money growth, encapsulated as M2, accelerated from 6.5 per cent in June 2025 to 12.4 per cent in May 2026, while inflation remained elevated through FY2025-26. The development financier predicted that the link between broad money and inflation may be strengthening, as monetary expansion increasingly coincides with persistent price pressures. The report suggests that monetary expansion may be contributing more directly to price pressures than in previous years, when the relationship between money-supply growth and inflation was described as less pronounced. The World Bank noted that growth in M2 has been driven by increases in both net domestic assets (NDA) and net foreign assets (NFA). Previously, moderation in money-supply growth was partly driven by substantial foreign-exchange sales by Bangladesh Bank (BB), but recent developments indicate a shift in the relationship between liquidity and prices.

cards.headline: Yelloway research collaboration develops fully fertile Cavendish banana

pages.text: Yelloway, a research collaboration between the banana company Chiquita and crop-improvement company KeyGene, announced this month that it has developed a fully fertile Cavendish banana. Because Cavendish bananas typically have three sets of chromosomes, they are usually sterile. The development of a fertile version may allow for cross-breeding to create new, commercially viable banana varieties that are resistant to disease. This follows reports of threats to the Cavendish, which is the variety most commonly found in global fruit bowls. Dr. Jose De Vega, an expert on crop genomics at the Earlham Institute in Norwich, noted that the Cavendish is under threat from diseases including Tropical Race 4 (TR4), a strain of Panama disease that has spread from Southeast Asia to Australia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America. De Vega cited a December 2025 report from Ecuador, the world's largest banana exporter, as a particularly worrying development regarding the disease. The threat to banana varieties impacts global supply chains and the food security of millions in the tropics who rely on bananas and plantains as a staple food and source of income. Globally, approximately 139 million tonnes of bananas are grown annually, making them the second most consumed fruit after the tomato.

cards.headline: Global food inflation expected to accelerate and persist through 2027

pages.text: Global food inflation is projected to accelerate in the coming months and continue into 2027 due to supply shocks including El Nino-driven droughts and war-related shipping disruptions. Maximo Torero, chief economist at the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), stated that the system is under considerable pressure and that impacts may increase toward the end of this year, the beginning of next year, and potentially throughout next year. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in a basket of internationally traded commodities, averaged 136 points in September, marking its highest reading since November 2022. According to the World Bank, food prices in the September quarter outpaced headline inflation in 22 percent of the 150 countries analyzed, an increase from 14 percent in the previous quarter.

Supply disruptions have impacted various commodities and regions. Attacks on Black Sea grain infrastructure have disrupted wheat shipments, affecting importers such as Egypt and Indonesia, while insecurity in the Red Sea has diverted vessels onto longer routes around Africa. Additionally, the US-Israeli war on Iran has raised fuel prices and disrupted fertilizer exports through the Strait of Hormuz. Environmental factors have also contributed to price increases, including the weakest monsoon in over a decade in India and dry El Nino weather in India and Southeast Asia. Specific price impacts include record high rice prices in Indonesia, a 25 percent increase in the cost of bread in Egypt, and all-time high sugar prices in India. The rising costs are noted to hit the world's poorest consumers hardest in low- and middle-income countries across West Asia, North Africa, and Asia.

cards.headline: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats and officials in West Bank

pages.text: Masked Israeli settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats and officials in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, according to reports from Arab News and The Guardian World. The incident occurred near the village of Taybeh, where a delegation including the French consul general in Jerusalem, the Belgian consul, and the Polish consul were participating in an olive harvest on lands belonging to the Christian town. Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Maxime Prévot condemned the violence, stating that the country would continue to push for European Union sanctions on settlers. Meanwhile, the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suggested the reports might be part of a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and its residents during the annual olive harvest.

cards.headline: TIB alleges state reforms in Bangladesh are being hindered by power politics and bureaucracy

pages.text: Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) stated in a statement on October 17, 2026, that the potential for establishing an accountable government system and reforming the state following the July mass uprising is being hindered by bureaucratic influence and power politics. TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman noted that while there was a commitment in the 31-point demand and election manifesto to implement state reforms and the July National Charter, uncertainty has arisen because members of parliament from the winning party did not take the oath as members of the proposed Constitutional Reform Commission. Iftekharuzzaman stated that the process of institutional reform, lawmaking, and constitutional amendment is now dependent on the inclinations of the ruling coalition. He further noted that of the 133 ordinances issued by the interim government, only those strengthening the executive branch have been passed into law, while ordinances intended to establish accountability have been suspended or repealed. TIB also reported that the opposition coalition is focused on partisan political interests rather than supporting state reform for the public interest.

The TIB statement raised several specific concerns regarding judicial and institutional independence. The organization questioned the government's role in ensuring judicial independence, noting that the repeal of the Supreme Court Judges Appointment Ordinance and the Supreme Court Secretariat (Amendment) Ordinance represents a stance opposed to state reform. Regarding the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC), TIB stated that failing to convert the ACC Amendment Ordinance into law and instead reverting to the 2004 law has obstructed efforts to overcome the commission's trust deficit. TIB also expressed concern over the National Human Rights Commission, stating that repealing its related ordinance to enact a new law conflicts with international standards and public aspirations for an independent commission. Additionally, the organization noted that the repeal of the Disappearances Prevention and Remedy Ordinance may protect agencies responsible for human rights violations. TIB criticized the decision to provide the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) with a new identity to make it more powerful instead of dissolving it, and noted that no initiatives have been taken to form an independent police commission despite political consensus. Finally, Iftekharuzzaman observed that despite a consensus on elected representatives publishing asset details within three months of assuming office, no such practices have been reflected since members of parliament were sworn in.

cards.headline: War in Yemen threatens archaeological sites and fuels antiquities trafficking concerns

pages.text: Renewed offensives by the Houthi militia in Yemen have raised concerns regarding the fate of cultural heritage following more than a decade of conflict, destruction, and looting. While the specific impact of recent fighting on museum collections and archaeological sites has yet to be established, researchers report significant damage to the country's history. Mohammed Ali Thamer, the director general of cultural statistics at the Sanaa-based Ministry of Culture, estimates that approximately 477 of the 2,318 archaeological sites documented by Yemen’s Archaeological Atlas in 2014 have undergone total or partial destruction during the war. Thamer’s research for the Sanaa Center, which utilizes ministry records, statistical data, and the Yemen Data Project, also documents 775 destructive operations affecting cultural sites between the start of the civil war in 2014 and 2025.

The conflict and fragmented authority have created conditions for the theft, smuggling, and sale of antiquities to international buyers. Thamer’s research describes a wave of looting during the current war, specifically targeting ancient tombs and archaeological sites in Marib, Al-Jawf, and Shabwa by individuals searching for gold and saleable artifacts. While comprehensive national statistics on stolen artifacts are unavailable, estimates in Thamer's research place the number of Yemeni artifacts held abroad between 10,000 and 14,000. Additionally, Yemen’s antiquities authorities have listed 8,000 objects they say were smuggled out during the war. Saleh Al-Baydani, president of the Anaween Center for Research and Transformation Studies in Aden, stated that the deterioration of state institutions has allowed trafficking to flourish.

cards.headline: Demands for transparency regarding GH¢49.7 million South Africa evacuation costs

pages.text: Akosua Manu, an advisor to NPP flagbearer Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has called for a transparent account of the GH¢49.7 million spent on an evacuation exercise of Ghanaian nationals from South Africa. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, October 13, Ms. Manu demanded answers regarding concerns over payment registers, alleged ghost names, and discrepancies in flight records, stating that the public deserves to know how the funds were used. She suggested that an independent audit should be welcomed if there is nothing to hide and argued that political disagreements regarding service passports should not distract from the financial scrutiny of the expenditure. This demand follows a public disagreement involving the Majority on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration Committee and its Deputy Ranking Member, Nana Asafo-Ayeh, concerning Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. The Majority has accused Mr. Asafo-Ayeh of character assassination following the Minister's refusal to grant a service passport to Nana Boakye, a former NPP National Youth Organiser and current NPP 2nd Vice Chairman. The Majority claims the Minister acted according to a presidential directive requiring the return of diplomatic and service passports. Salaga South MP Zuwera Ibrahimah Mohammed defended the Minister, stating public officials must operate within the law regarding requests for favors.

The Majority Caucus of the Parliamentary Select Committee on Foreign Affairs has dismissed allegations that funds used to evacuate 1,964 Ghanaian nationals from South Africa remain unaccounted for. During a press conference on October 12, 2026, the Committee Chairman, Dr. Alfred Oko Vanderpuije, stated that the committee received and scrutinized a comprehensive report from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Dr. Vanderpuije noted that on September 18, 2026, the Committee received a report accompanied by an exhaustive roll of all 1,964 evacuees, which included names, dates of birth, passport numbers, professions, contact information, amounts received, and signatures. He stated that not a single name is missing or unaccounted for. The Chairman added that the Ministry provided extensive financial documentation, including receipts for chartered flights, commercial airline tickets, transportation, feeding, accommodation, and other logistics managed by Ghana’s High Commission in South Africa. The documentation also reportedly included evidence of a GH¢16 million donation from Ibrahim Mahama’s Engineers and Planners. These statements were made in response to a press conference held by the Minority Caucus on October 11, 2026, which alleged that substantial sums of public funds used for the evacuation were unaccounted for.

cards.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine received no early warning of Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv

pages.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine received no early warning from partners regarding a Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv on October 12, 2026. Zelenskyy described the attack, in which five missiles hit civilian infrastructure, as “particularly vile” and noted that receiving intelligence from western allies is critical for preventing deaths. While he did not apportion blame for the lack of warning, he stated that Russia “did not heed” the call for a ceasefire made by US President Donald Trump. 13 October 2026 reporting indicates that while US officials had threatened to halt intelligence sharing with Kyiv over the weekend, Trump denied that sharing had stopped, telling reporters that the US is sharing intelligence and working with both Ukraine and Russia to end the war. Trump has previously demanded that Ukraine cease attacks on Russian oil refineries and has blamed Zelenskyy for rising fuel prices in the US. Despite speculations regarding intelligence ties, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha insisted that intelligence cooperation with the US has continued.
